body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：搜尋服務把 HNSW 的 `efSearch` 由 20 調到 200。幾條 demo query 的第一個結果好咗，團隊話可以把 setting 拉到最大。你會點樣決定 ANN config？
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：把 `efSearch` 加高，直到 top result 看起來正確；慢咗再加機器。

呢個答案知道搜尋準確度可以調，卻未說明自己量度咗乜。**Approximate nearest-neighbour search，ANN** 不承諾每次都找出全庫真正最近的 k 個 vector。它用 index 結構縮細候選範圍，換取比逐一比較所有 vector 更快的查詢。HNSW、IVF 或其他 index 都有近似程度、memory、build cost 和 query latency 的取捨；某個 config 在小 sample 夠好，未必在較難 query、metadata filter 或 traffic peak 下仍然成立。

## 先知道你為何接受近似

把 ANN 想成在一個很大的圖書館找書。逐個書架看一次，最有機會找齊最相關的書，但很慢；一張捷徑地圖帶你到幾個可能的區域，通常快得多，但偶爾會錯過藏在另一區的好書。`efSearch` 可以粗略理解為容許捷徑地圖多看多少候選。它不是 quality 開關，也不是每一條 query 都同樣受益。

先建立一個 exact baseline。在同一份 frozen corpus snapshot、同一個 embedding receipt、同一個 metric 和同一條 filter 下，讓 brute-force search 算出 exact top-k；再比較 ANN candidate 是否保留那些結果。這給你 **recall@k**：exact top-k 裡有多少仍然被 ANN 找到。但 ANN recall 不是 user relevance。仍要有一組由人確認 expected evidence 的 query，分開記錄「找不到原本最近的 vector」與「找到了 vector 但它不適用」。

## 不要只在一個平均數裡決定

把 query 分 slice：短語、較長 domain term、罕見條款、相似但錯的文件、不同 corpus size，以及 low／high-selectivity metadata filters。對每個 candidate config 同時記錄 recall@k、evidence coverage、p50/p95/p99 retrieval latency、memory、index build time、filter fallback、timeout 和 cost proxy。一個 setting 可能令平均 recall 上升，卻令有 filter 的 p99 突然變差；另一個可能快，卻在罕見 domain term 漏掉唯一有用的文件。這些都是不同的 decision，不應該被「top result 睇落唔錯」合併。

設定一份 route budget：例如互動 route 有 latency guardrail，後台 analysis route 可以容許較高 `efSearch` 或 async exact verification。若 candidate 未過某個 critical-query coverage gate，保留簡單 baseline、縮窄 corpus、交人手，或讓該 route 不使用 ANN。加 machine 可能合理，但要先看慢的是 index traversal、filter、network 還是 queue；否則只係把錯誤設定跑得更快。

## 可以讓人重播的決定

建立 `ann-recall-budget-lab`：

- `fixtures/corpus-snapshot.jsonl`：虛構 chunk、embedding receipt、metadata 和 source version。
- `fixtures/query-slices.jsonl`：固定 query、filter、expected evidence、critical 標記和拒答 case。
- `scripts/compare-exact-and-ann.mjs`：在 deterministic synthetic vectors 上輸出 exact／ANN top-k、recall@k 和 route timing。
- `evidence/config-comparison.md`：列 candidate config、每個 slice 的 coverage、p95/p99、memory 與拒絕理由。
- `docs/retrieval-budget.md`：說明哪條 route 可以慢、哪條不能漏、何時 fallback 和誰收 review。

面試時可以說：我不是把 ANN parameter 調到最大；我會用 exact baseline 定義近似損失，再用 user evidence、tail latency 和 route budget 決定哪個 config 值得保留。

## 延伸閱讀

[Similarity 高，點解仍然拎錯文件？](/zh-HK/interview-lab/high-similarity-is-not-relevance)、[加 GPU 前先 trace p99 latency](/zh-HK/interview-lab/trace-p99-latency-before-adding-gpus) 和 [RAG Index、Chunk、Rerank 同 Cache：每一層都可以搵錯證據](/zh-HK/articles/retrieval-index-chunk-rerank-and-cache)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。index、vectors、query、config、traces、metrics、artefact 和結果全是虛構 synthetic 本地草稿材料；不歸屬任何公司，亦不代表任何公司現時或過去的面試流程、live system 或 production outcome。

把 ANN 想成在很大的图书馆找书。逐个书架看一次，最有机会找齐最相关的书，但很慢；一张捷径地图带你到几个可能的区域，通常快得多，但偶尔会错过藏在另一区的好书。`efSearch` 可以粗略理解为容许捷径地图多看多少候选。它不是 quality 开关，也不是每条 query 都同样受益。

把 query 分 slice：短语、较长 domain term、罕见条款、相似但错误的文件、不同 corpus size，以及 low／high-selectivity metadata filters。对每个 candidate config 同时记录 recall@k、evidence coverage、p50/p95/p99 retrieval latency、memory、index build time、filter fallback、timeout 与 cost proxy。一个 setting 可能让平均 recall 上升，却让有 filter 的 p99 突然变差；另一个可能快，却在罕见 domain term 漏掉唯一有用的文件。这些是不同 decision，不该被“top result 看起来不错”合并。

- `fixtures/corpus-snapshot.jsonl`：虚构 chunk、embedding receipt、metadata 与 source version。
- `fixtures/query-slices.jsonl`：固定 query、filter、expected evidence、critical 标记与拒答 case。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: A search service raises HNSW `efSearch` from 20 to 200. The first result improves for a few demo queries, and the team wants to set the value as high as possible. How would you choose an ANN configuration?
>
> Half-right answer: Increase `efSearch` until the top result looks right, then add machines if it becomes slow.

This answer recognises that search accuracy is tunable, but it has not said what was measured. **Approximate nearest-neighbour search**, or ANN, does not promise the true nearest k vectors from the whole corpus on every query. It uses an index structure to reduce the candidate set, trading some exactness for a faster query than comparing every vector. HNSW, IVF, and related indexes each trade approximation, memory, build cost, and query latency. A configuration that looks good on a small sample may not hold for harder queries, metadata filters, or a traffic peak.

## Know why approximation is acceptable

Think of ANN as finding a book in a very large library. Reading every shelf gives the best chance of finding all relevant books, but is slow. A shortcut map takes you to likely sections much faster, but may miss a useful book in another area. `efSearch` roughly determines how many candidates that shortcut map is allowed to inspect. It is not a quality switch, and every query does not benefit equally.

Create an exact baseline first. On the same frozen corpus snapshot, embedding receipt, metric, and filter, use brute-force search to compute exact top-k, then compare whether an ANN candidate retains those results. That yields **recall@k**: how much of exact top-k ANN finds. ANN recall is not user relevance, though. Keep a human-checked query set with expected evidence so that you can distinguish failing to find the nearest vector from finding a vector that is not applicable.

## Do not decide inside one average

Slice the queries into short phrases, longer domain terms, rare clauses, similar-but-wrong documents, corpus sizes, and low- or high-selectivity metadata filters. For every candidate configuration, record recall@k, evidence coverage, p50/p95/p99 retrieval latency, memory, index build time, filter fallback, timeout, and a cost proxy. One setting may improve average recall while suddenly worsening filtered p99. Another may be fast while missing the only useful document for a rare domain term. Those are separate decisions, not one claim that the top result looked good.

Set a route budget. An interactive route can have a latency guardrail; a back-office analysis route may permit a higher `efSearch` or asynchronous exact verification. If a candidate misses a critical-query coverage gate, retain a simple baseline, narrow the corpus, hand off to a person, or do not use ANN for that route. More machines may be valid, but first establish whether index traversal, filtering, network, or queueing is slow. Otherwise you only run the wrong configuration faster.

## A decision someone can replay

Build `ann-recall-budget-lab` with:

- `fixtures/corpus-snapshot.jsonl` containing fictional chunks, embedding receipts, metadata, and source versions.
- `fixtures/query-slices.jsonl` containing fixed queries, filters, expected evidence, critical flags, and abstention cases.
- `scripts/compare-exact-and-ann.mjs` writing exact/ANN top-k, recall@k, and route timing for deterministic synthetic vectors.
- `evidence/config-comparison.md` listing candidate configurations, per-slice coverage, p95/p99, memory, and rejection reasons.
- `docs/retrieval-budget.md` stating which route may be slow, which must not miss evidence, when fallback occurs, and who receives review.

In an interview, you can say: I would not tune an ANN parameter to the maximum. I would use an exact baseline to define approximation loss, then use user evidence, tail latency, and the route budget to decide which configuration earns its place.

## Further reading

[High similarity is not relevance](/en/interview-lab/high-similarity-is-not-relevance), [Trace p99 latency before adding GPUs](/en/interview-lab/trace-p99-latency-before-adding-gpus), and [RAG index, chunks, reranking, and cache: every layer can find the wrong evidence](/en/articles/retrieval-index-chunk-rerank-and-cache).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG standalone practice prompt. Indexes, vectors, queries, configurations, traces, metrics, artefacts, and results are fictional synthetic local-draft material. No company is attributed, and this is not evidence of any company’s current or past interview process, a live system, or a production outcome.
